quote: Additionally, an association of immune-related CALHM6/FAM26F, PARM1, BTNL2, and TNFSF15 genes, as well as NPHS1, which encodes nephrin expressed in podocytes, has been identified as a locus that achieves genome-wide significance in pediatric SSNS.
summary: Review of nephrotic syndrome genetics noting a GWAS association of CALHM6 with pediatric steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome; nothing on UC.

quote: Some of these genes were observed in all forms of the disease (CD2, CD27, chit1, FA2H, FAM26F, GZMB, MMP9, SLAMF7, UBD) and others were exclusive to reactional forms (Type "1" reaction: GPNMB, IL1B, MICAL2, FOXQ1; Type "2" reaction: AKR1B10, FAM180B, FOXQ1, NNMT, NR1D1, PTX3, TNFRSF25).
summary: FAM26F is one of many differentially expressed mRNAs in leprosy skin lesions; no UC data and no gene-specific result.

quote: Thus, these 92 genes (including TNFAIP6 , GZMB , S100A8 , CSF2 , CLEC4E , S100A9 , IL1RN , FCGR1A , CLIC3 , CD14 , PLA2G7 , FAM26F , IL3RA , NKG7 , IL32 , CCL3 , OLR1 , LILRA4 , APOC1 , MYBL2 , and others; Supplementary file 3 ) nominate a signature of anticipatory markers of anti-TNF therapy outcome in newly diagnosed patients and are validated in one internal (bulk RNA-seq from PREDICT patients) and two external (RISK and E-MTAB-7604) bulk RNA-seq cohorts.
summary: FAM26F is one of 92 genes in a pediatric Crohn's baseline signature associated with anti-TNF outcome; no result specific to this gene.

quote: Conversely, Calhm6 deficiency leads to suppressed Creb1 activity, which in turn augments M1-like macrophage polarization, enhancing bactericidal activity and the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
summary: Calhm6 deficiency in macrophages promotes M1 polarization and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while Calhm6-bearing ectosomes suppress LPS-induced inflammation, so Calhm6 limits inflammation; no UC model tested.

quote: A cis-expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) has been identified, showing that the minor protective allele is associated with increased expression of CALHM6 [ 39 ].
summary: Review of nephrotic syndrome genetics describing a CALHM6 GWAS locus and eQTL where the protective allele raises CALHM6 expression; not about UC.

quote: In total, 9 MCI signatures ( IL1B , IL8 , IL6 , PTGS2 , IL1A , CCL2 , TNF , CXCL3 , and CXCL1 ) and 12 MC signatures ( CXCL11 , CXCL10 , CXCL9 , TNFSF10 , HLA-DQA1 , FCN1 , IGFBP4 , HLA-DPB1 , HLA-DQB1 , FAM26F , RGL1 , and CD4 ) were found to be upregulated, which were subsequently used to calculate a signature score for each monocyte in the single-cell RNA sequencing data sets of patients.
summary: FAM26F appears only in a 12-gene monocyte signature list in a trained immunity review; no gene-specific finding.

quote: A set of genes including CALHM6 , HCP5 , PRRG4 , DDX60L , and RASA2 exhibited high weighted degree centrality, implicating them as influential hubs that exert strong influence over various genetic traits 37 .
summary: CALHM6 is listed as a network hub dark gene across many diseases, without a UC-specific or gene-specific experimental result.

quote: Further network analysis of dark genes, including  CALHM6, HCP5, PRRG4, DDX60L and  RASA2, revealed a notably high weighted degree of association with genetic diseases and phenotypes.
summary: Network analysis lists CALHM6 among dark genes with high connectivity to many diseases, including UC among shared linkages, without a specific result.

quote: These groups were represented as a heatmap ( Figure 1A ), and included several histocompatibility two genes (e.g., Egr1 , Egr2 , Stat1 , and Stat2 ) and phagocytic receptor genes (e.g., Axl , Clec7a , CD36 , Clec1a , Fcgr4 , Clec3b , Clec4a1 , Anxa3 , Anxa4 , and Anxa5 ).
summary: Clec1a is only named in a list of phagocytic receptor genes in aging mouse microglia; unrelated to UC.

quote: Central to initiation of protective antifungal immunity are members of the CLR superfamily which include Dectin-1 (CLEC7A), Dectin-2 (CLEC4N), macrophage C-type lectin (MCL, CLEC4D), macrophage-inducible C-type lectin (Mincle, CLEC4E), mannose receptor (MR, CD206), dendritic cell-specific intercellular adhesion molecule-3-grabbing nonintegrin (DC-SIGN, CD209), and melanin-sensing C-type lectin (MelLec, CLEC1A) [ 9 ].
summary: Review of C-type lectin receptors in antifungal T cell immunity that names CLEC1A (MelLec) as a melanin sensor; no UC content.

quote: CLEC-1 plays a role in antifungal immunity, since this receptor recognize the naphthalene-diol unit of 1,8-dihydroxynaphthalene (DHN)-melanin, a component found in conidial spores of A. fumigatus as well as in other DHN-melanized fungi (Stappers et al, 2018 ).
summary: Review of Dectin cluster receptors describing CLEC-1 as a melanin receptor needed for antifungal immunity; no UC data.

quote: On the other hand, ITIM‐containing CLRs, including DCIR, recruit a tyrosine phosphatase such as SHP‐1 or SHP‐2 to ITIM and inhibit tyrosine phosphorylation, thereby blocking signals induced by PRRs and cytokines. 4 , 5 , 6 However, DCIR also transduces a positive signal to sustain type 1‐IFNR–induced STAT1 activation in DCs. 7 By contrast, CLEC1A and LOX‐1 contain no known signaling motifs.
summary: Review of myeloid C-type lectin receptors in mucosal and skin disease that mentions CLEC1A only as lacking known signaling motifs.

quote: In SOLAR, PFNA demonstrated significant positive associations with the largest number of proteins, including ACP5, CLEC1A, HMOX1, LRP11, MCAM, SPARCL1, and SSC5D.
summary: CLEC1A is one of several plasma proteins positively associated with PFNA exposure in Hispanic youth; unrelated to UC.

quote: Another shared locus is CLEC1A, where the direction of effects is aligned, that encodes a lectin involved in cell signaling, and the anti-fungal immune response.
summary: CLEC1A is a locus shared between severe COVID-19 and SLE GWAS signals with aligned effect direction; no UC data.

quote: CLRs, recognizing carbohydrates, activate pathways through MINCLE and CLEC1A, influencing phagocytosis and inflammation.
summary: Review of microbiota and inflammation mentions CLEC1A only in passing as a lectin receptor influencing phagocytosis and inflammation.

quote: During corneal Aspergillus fumigatus infection, CCPG1 expression increases and co-localizes with the inhibitory receptor CLEC-1 in macrophages, suggesting that they may synergistically regulate macrophage function in inflammatory responses, but the specific interaction remains to be studied ( 154 ).
summary: ER-phagy review notes CCPG1 co-localizes with CLEC-1 in macrophages during corneal fungal infection; no UC content.

quote: Many C-type lectins have been identified on DCs: (1) Type I multi-CRD lectins are represented by the mannose receptor (Sallusto et al. 1995 ) and DEC-205 (Kato et al. 2000 ); and (2) type II single-CRD lectins by DC-SIGN, dectin-1, dectin-2, Langerin, BCDA-2, DCIR, DLEC, CLEC-1, and DC-ASGPR (Geijtenbeek et al. 2000a ) (10.1007/978-3-7091-1065-2_35).
summary: CLEC-1 appears only in a list of type II C-type lectins found on dendritic cells in a book chapter.

quote: Immunofluorescence showed the colocalization of CCPG1 and CLEC-1 in THP-1 macrophages.
summary: In a corneal fungal infection cell model, CLEC-1 colocalizes with CCPG1 in THP-1 macrophages; the study concerns CCPG1 and is not about colitis.

quote: In this study, we found that Clec1a-/- mice develop milder symptoms upon induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), an animal model for multiple sclerosis.
summary: Clec1a knockout mice have milder EAE with lower IL-17 and weaker dendritic cell antigen presentation, so Clec1a promotes neuroinflammation; colitis was not tested.

quote: The two most significant genes in our SKAT-O rare variant analysis after NOD2 , VWA2 and HAPLN3 , are also extracellular matrix components.
summary: HAPLN3 was among the top genes in rare-variant exome association analysis of pediatric IBD, with no direction of effect stated.

quote: The SVM-RFE algorithm was also adopted to identify 13 genes from DEGs as diagnostic signatures, specifically ITGA4, BTN3A3, SLFN11, EPSTI1, CD86, HAPLN3, CD38, CWH43, ACP5, PLAC8, MPEG1, KRT20, and MCUB.
summary: HAPLN3 is one of 13 SVM-RFE candidate genes in an interstitial cystitis study and was not among the final diagnostic markers; unrelated to UC.

quote: Six putative NIPs did not co-precipitate with NOD2 in these conditions (DOCK7, PPP2R3B, IKBIP, CHMP5, C10orf67, PRR16) ( Fig 2B ).
summary: IKBIP was a putative NOD2 interactor from a yeast two-hybrid screen that failed to co-precipitate with NOD2; no IBD result specific to it.

quote: Moreover, IKIP-deficient mice were more susceptible to LPS-induced septic shock and dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis.
summary: IKIP negatively regulates NF-kB by blocking IKK phosphorylation, and IKIP-deficient mice develop worse DSS colitis, so IKIP is protective.

quote: By competitively binding IKIP, WNT2B reduced the binding of IKIP to IKKβ and promoted the activation of the NF-κB pathway.
summary: WNT2B in IBD macrophages binds IKIP and displaces it from IKKb to activate NF-kB; IKIP itself was not perturbed, so its own direction is not tested.

quote: Subsequently, we developed a RiskScore model based on six H. pylori -associated genes (TNFRSF1B, CTLA4, ABCA1, IKBIP, AKAP5, and NPC2) and observed that the high-risk patients exhibited poor prognosis, higher suppressive immune infiltration, and were closely associated with cancer activation-related pathways.
summary: IKBIP is one of six genes in a stomach adenocarcinoma prognostic risk score; unrelated to UC and with no gene-specific result.
